sents.t: In August, Carlos invited Lily and me on a camping trip with Ana at Pine Lake.
“If the weather is good, we’ll swim and fish,” he said.
“If it rains, we’ll play cards in the tent.”
The forecast said sunny, so I didn’t pack my rain jacket.
Big mistake.
The first night was perfect.
We grilled corn, told ghost stories, and fell asleep to the sound of frogs.
But at three in the morning, I woke up to a strange noise.
Something was opening our cooler!
I turned on my flashlight.
Two raccoons looked at me, holding our hot dogs.
“If you chase them, they’ll just come back,” Carlos whispered.
“Make noise.” We banged pots until they ran away, but our breakfast was gone.
The next afternoon, a storm came.
The rain was so heavy that water came into our tent, and our sleeping bags got soaked.
Carlos’s “waterproof” tent wasn’t waterproof at all.
We threw everything into the car, wet and muddy, and drove to a diner.
Over hot pancakes, we couldn’t stop laughing.
“Next time, if we go camping, we’ll check the forecast twice,” Lily said.
“And we’ll lock the cooler,” Ana added.

comp.q: What did Carlos plan to do if it rained?
comp.fa: اگر باران می‌بارید، کارلوس برنامه داشت چه کار کنند؟

What woke Sam up at three in the morning?

comp.q: What was wrong with the tent?
What will they do next time?
o: check the forecast twice and lock the cooler
comp.fa: دفعه‌ی بعد چه کار خواهند کرد؟
